CapEx in the US is skyrocketing:

The value of US nondefense capital goods shipments, excluding aircraft, jumped +11.6% YoY in September, reaching a record $86 billion.

This marks the fastest annual growth rate since July 2021.

Even more impressive, shipments have risen at a 3-month annualized rate of +16.5%, the strongest pace since 2011, excluding the pandemic recovery.

Since October 2024, shipments have increased by +$12 billion, or +16.5%.

Much of this momentum is being fueled by the AI investment boom.

Orders for computers, servers, storage devices, and related equipment have surged +27% YoY, the largest annual increase since January 1997.

The AI infrastructure buildout is beyond massive.

US mortgage demand is down to historic lows:

US purchase mortgage applications index fell -2% last week, to 131 points, its 2nd-lowest since January 2025.

This also marks the 6th-lowest weekly reading since 1995, down -32% since January.

As a result, US mortgage applications are now -50% below the pre-pandemic levels seen in 2019.

This comes as the 30Y fixed mortgage rate has risen +120 basis points since February, to 7.18%, near its highest since November 2023.

Rates have now been above 7.0% for 7 consecutive weeks.

The US housing market is frozen.

By comparison, the 20-day average oscillated around 4 million contracts in 2022.

8 of the 10 highest daily put option volume readings have occurred in 2026.

We are seeing unprecedented options activity right now.

tweets.text:
Thanks for engaging, @bchesky. I don’t presume you could never offer a price-match guarantee. You could, and so could Booking, Expedia and every other OTA which is part of my point. If agents check every major OTA by default, discovery matters less and more of the decision comes down to a price comparison at the last step. A price match may well keep the booking on Airbnb, but it does so by moving some of the surplus to the guest and, over time, to whoever owns the agent. I’m not arguing that agents cut Airbnb out, or that Airbnb or Booking go to zero. I’m pointing out that this could lower Airbnb’s economic profit and make it harder to keep compounding its earnings over the long term.

On apps, I actually didn’t design one, and I’m not suggesting people will want to. I spoke to Muse for about 30 seconds, it built the page, and I gave it some feedback over a couple of hours while walking with my son. That’s possible TODAY. In 3-5 years, I would expect the first version to need much less tweaking, so this may not remain just a hobbyist thing. And I agree I couldn’t design an app better than Airbnb’s. But the agent’s page doesn’t need to beat Airbnb’s app. It only needs to be good enough while showing me the price on every major OTA out there, which Airbnb’s app/agent is unlikely to do.
tweets.quoted_tweet_text: @borrowed_ideas You presume we could never offer a price-match guarantee. You also assume people will want to design their own apps (other than hobbyists, unlikely), and I am willing to bet even you won't be able to design an app better than us (but if you can, come work for us).
